bx_meta.note: Postgres player_statistics + team_statistics, 2003-04 on; possessions = team/opponent average x minute share; shading = percentile among players with 500+ minutes (regular season, scaled by games played) or 100+ (playoffs)

cmp_meta.method:
(per player S, candidates C = rated hub players with 3,000+ career minutes):
  age       age on Feb 1 of the season (hub convention), floored to an integer to align curves.
  value     sum over seasons of max(0, r + 2) x minutes / 3000  (points above a -2 replacement level, per full season).
  peak      mean of the best 3 seasons with 1,000+ minutes (fewer if he has fewer).
  shape     minutes-weighted RMS gap between the two rating-by-age curves over the ages both have; S's curve is extended
            by his 5-season forecast (weight 600 minutes each) so rookies and young players have a shape to match.
  tiers     elite = top 50 all-time by value or by peak (full careers); goat = top 15 by value.
            elite S -> candidates restricted to elite players sharing a position group (G / F / C; dual positions count
            in both); goat S -> candidates from the top 30 by value, any position, same group preferred.
  score     shape / 1.5 + |value gap at S's age| / value scale + |peak gap at S's age| / 2 + position penalty
            - small bonuses for a long career (recognisable) and for having played on past S's age (shows what came next).
Ghost forecasts: direct ridge-free least squares, one per horizon h = 1..5: r(t+h) ~ reliability-weighted mean of the last
  three seasons, the reliability itself, age spline at t, log minutes at t. Fit on targets <= 2015; evaluated on origins
  2016+ with targets <= 2025. Spread = residual SD by horizon and minutes band.

upc_meta.note: Projected line = Singular rest-of-season projection x the adjustments that beat the plain average on 2023-24 and 2024-25 games. Range = 80% for a single game. Schedule snapshot is static: the list does not update after the page is built.

persistence.read: share of one season's swing that carries into the next, roughly; the rest is noise and context

hof_meta.label: hof_features.csv is_hof (curated inductees as players)
hof_meta.model: standardized logistic regression (C=0.5); 80% range = 10th-90th percentile over 60 player-bootstrap refits (model uncertainty only)
hof_meta.note: Chance of induction given the resume after each completed season; it already prices the typical rest of a career for someone with that resume at that age. Trained on players whose last season started by 2014. Seasons through 2025-26 only.

splits_meta.diff: diff[measure] = [raw, lo80, hi80, believable]. raw = group a minus group b. lo80/hi80 = 10th/90th percentile of the diff over 1000 bootstrap resamples of the player's games (fixed seed). diff = null when either side has < 5 games.
splits_meta.believable_rule: believable = raw x rel. rel = Spearman-Brown reliability for this player's minutes: rel = k r / (1 + (k - 1) r), k = his season minutes / 1928 (median minutes in the test sample), r = the split x measure year-to-year correlation below; rel = 0 when r <= 0. At typical starter minutes rel ~ r. 'rel' is stored per split. Nothing else is shrunk.

persistence_test.design: Seasons 2012-13 .. 2024-25; player-season pairs (t, t+1) with >= 1000 minutes in both; diff computed as above in each season (>= 5 games per side). r = Pearson r(diff_t, diff_t+1). lo80/hi80 = 10th/90th percentile over 1000 bootstrap resamples of players (all of a player's pairs move together). 2025-26 not used. mean_diff/sd_diff = across all qualifying player-seasons. r_same_team / r_moved = r for pairs where his main team (most minutes) was the same / different in t and t+1: a split that persists only for same-team pairs is a team or arena effect, not a player trait.
persistence_test.read: r estimates how much of an observed one-season split repeats next season. r near 0 means the individual split is mostly noise even if the league-wide mean is real.

rules.rank: all-time among every player in the DB, regular season
rules.pass_next: [person_id, name, career total, is current player] for the next three above him now
rules.proj: [p10, median, p90] final career total from 2,000 simulated careers
rules.proj_rank: rank of the median projected total against everyone's CURRENT totals (other active players will also grow)
rules.next: [{m: milestone, p: calibrated P(reach), p_raw: simulated P(reach)}] for the next two round numbers; p = recalibration map in meta.recalibration applied to p_raw
rules.model: survival draw U~Unif: active in season s iff U < P(s) (no comebacks); games per active season drawn from his last 4 seasons' games (scaled to 82; weights .4/.3/.2/.1) + N(0,5), cap 82, x (1 - 0.02 per year past 30); per-game rate starts at his 2025-26 + 2026-27 per-game and steps each season by the age-curve median log change + noise (age-curve residual sd; shared component across stats, rho .6). Current season counts only the remaining share of team games (0.854).

backtest.design: held out: freeze at end of 2015-16; age curve, survival kernel (pool 1996-97..2007-08) and hazard refit on data through 2015-16; cohort = played 2015-16 with 3+ seasons; projection truncated at 2025-26; actual = totals through 2025-26. Noise scale tuned on a separate 2008-09 -> 2015-16 freeze.
backtest.naive: 2015-16 per-game x 2015-16 games x seasons through 2025-26 at age <= 35

recalibration.fit: 2015-16 freeze backtest (10-season horizon), next-milestone rows, all stats pooled; logistic MLE
recalibration.caveat: fit on 10-season-horizon outcomes; current probabilities are full-career, so the map is assumed to transfer. Bins: [n, mean predicted, observed rate]. Brier in 'brier'.

findings.rule: Only tests the registry marks supported or mixed. Excluded as null/failed or untested: hot hand, FT pressure, playoff effort, clutch, screen value, SLAP aging, singularity, role capacity ranking, trade prices, handler stacking, fluidity, two-foul.
notes: Rim deterrence: S/data/features/rim_defense.parquet lam_rate is constant 1000 in every row (it is the shrinkage lambda, not a value), so rim_rate is used; it is lineup-adjusted and z-scaled. Negative rim_rate = fewer opponent rim attempts; the value is sign-flipped so higher = more deterrence.

Rim deterrence verdict id: the inventory gives no registry id (it says 'production SiPM input'); SP11 (supported held out) and LR30f10c test this input. LR30f10 (young-big gap) is not supported and is not used.
E38b: registry status 'supported' but strength field 'null' (no held-out label); shown as 'supported'.
T15 registry strength is 'held out' (inventory: 'supported but weak'); weak = R2 0.14.
Usage choice percentile is the file's own disc_rel_pct.
